D: A Pakistani-American comic falls for a grad student who falls seriously ill, and gets to know her parents at the hospital.
P: Serve the mains when Kumail's mum sits him down to family dinner with yet another surprise guest.
S: Thin oven roasted chips with masala spice

Crisp oven fries tossed hot with chaat masala, chilli and lime, scattered with coriander and red onion, a cool mint yoghurt for dipping. Heat the oven to 220C. Cut 1kg potatoes into thin chips, soak 20 minutes, drain and dry well. Toss with 3 tbsp oil and roast 35 minutes on lined trays, turning once, until crisp. Toss hot with 2 tsp chaat masala, half a tsp chilli powder, salt and the juice of half a lime. Scatter with chopped coriander and finely diced red onion. Blend 200g Greek yoghurt with a handful of mint and a pinch of salt for dipping.
Fried pastry triangles of spiced potato, peas and onion

Spiced potato, peas and onion folded into pastry triangles, fried at 180C until crisp, with mint and coriander chutney. Boil and crush 600g potatoes with 150g peas, fried onion and a spoon of garam masala. Cut spring roll pastry into strips, fill and fold into triangles. Fry at 180C until crisp. Blitz mint and coriander with a little water, lemon and salt for chutney.
Hospital cafeteria toasties with tomato soup
Kumail stuck in the hospital cafeteria with Emily's parents

Cheddar and mozzarella toasties grilled crisp in butter and cut into dippers, with shots of roasted tomato and basil soup on the side. Roast 1kg halved tomatoes, 1 onion in wedges and 4 garlic cloves with oil and salt at 200C for 35 minutes. Blitz with 400ml stock and a handful of basil, simmer 5 minutes and season. Fill 8 slices of white bread with 120g grated cheddar and 80g grated mozzarella, butter the outsides and cook in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes a side. Cut into fingers and serve with the soup in small cups.
M: Yoghurt marinated chicken layered with basmati and crisp fried onions
Chicken thighs marinated in yoghurt and spices, layered with par-cooked basmati, fried onions and saffron milk, sealed and baked at 170C for 45 minutes.

A thick, buttery crust pressed up the sides of a deep tin, layered with mozzarella, fennel sausage and chunky garlic tomato sauce, baked until bubbling. Mix 400g plain flour, 7g yeast, 1 tsp salt, 60g melted butter and 230ml warm water, knead 5 minutes and rest 1 hour. Heat the oven to 220C. Press into an oiled 28cm cake tin and up the sides. Layer 300g sliced mozzarella, then 400g Italian sausage meat in flat patches. Simmer 400g crushed tomatoes with 2 garlic cloves and oregano for 10 minutes and spread over the top. Scatter 40g parmesan and bake 30 to 35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
W: Basmati rice simmered in milk with sugar and cardamom, served warm
Rice simmered slowly in milk with cardamom and sugar until creamy, served warm or chilled with pistachios.
K: Black tea simmered with ginger, cardamom, cinnamon and milk

Black tea simmered with milk, ginger, cardamom and cinnamon, sweetened and strained into cups. Bring 500ml water to the boil with sliced ginger, a few crushed cardamom pods and a cinnamon stick. Add 4 black tea bags and simmer 2 minutes. Pour in 500ml milk and raw sugar to taste, simmer 5 minutes more and strain into cups.

Slice the onions and fry in the oil until crisp.
Par-cook the basmati for a few minutes and drain.
Layer the chicken, rice and onions in a heavy pot and drizzle with saffron soaked in the warm milk.
Seal the pot and bake at 170C.

m.note: Yoghurt marinated chicken layered with basmati and crisp fried onions
m.how: Marinate 1kg chicken thighs in yoghurt and garam masala for 2 hours. Fry 2 sliced onions until crisp. Par-cook 400g basmati for 5 minutes. Layer chicken, rice and onions in a pot, drizzle with saffron soaked in warm milk, seal and bake at 170C for 45 minutes.

w.note: Basmati rice simmered in milk with sugar and cardamom, served warm
w.how: Simmer 100g basmati rice in 1.5L milk over low heat, stirring often, for 45 minutes until thick and creamy. Stir in 100g sugar and a pinch of ground cardamom. Serve warm or chilled with chopped pistachios scattered on top.
